title: The way of the Church (Redemptor Hominis 14)
hookLine: the human person is the way for the Church
tomorrow: a tired fisherman is told to try again, farther out. why?

cards: Every big organization has a road map: the five-year plan, the strategy slides, the growth chart with the arrow going up.
Pope John Paul II, in an encyclical called Redemptor Hominis, named the road a whole church has to travel. It isn't on any chart. It's a person.

teach.h: THE CHURCH CANNOT ABANDON THE PERSON.
teach.b: Paragraph fourteen opens with a refusal: the Church cannot abandon the human person. Then the image.

teach.h: THE PRIMARY ROUTE IS A PERSON.
teach.b: The human person, John Paul II writes, is the primary route the Church must travel in carrying out its mission, a way traced out by Christ himself. And which person? Not humanity in the abstract.
The real, concrete, historical person: each one, in the unrepeatable reality of who they are, with their mind and will, their conscience and heart.
He leans on a line from last week, Gaudium et Spes 22: by becoming human, Christ united himself in some way with every person.
If God took that road to each person, the Church can't take a shortcut around anyone.

And it gathers these two weeks into one picture: a kitchen table, a call to love, a conscience, a family of peoples, a freedom no one may force, siblings across churches, a bakery shift, a sending, a witness.
Every one of them ran through a person.

how: Catholic teaching often cites this line when it speaks of care for the poor, the sick and each person's dignity, from parishes to hospitals to schools.

games.q: what does “the way of the church” mean?
o: the customs a parish follows on Sunday
the human person, the road the Church must travel
a pilgrim route walked to visit holy places

games.q: the way of the church — tap the pairs.
p: the Church cannot abandon the person
each person as they really are

s: 'the way of the Church' means its rules and customs
the encyclical names the human person as its primary way.
John Paul II builds on Gaudium et Spes 22 here
Christ united himself in some way with every person.
Redemptor Hominis says the Church's road is humanity in the abstract
the real, concrete, historical person, each one.

games.q: a busy hospital volunteer team wants to stop bedside visits and send every patient one group message instead. what does Redemptor Hominis 14 say?
o: the concrete person is the road; no shortcuts.
efficiency is the Church's first way.
humanity in general matters more than one patient.
games.why: John Paul II calls the real, concrete person, each one, the primary route the Church must travel. a group message is a shortcut around the person.

practice: Say aloud, slowly, the name of one person you'll see tomorrow, the way you'd want your own name said. Then add one thing about them nobody else has: a laugh, a habit, a worry they carry.
Rest there, with one unrepeatable person in mind.

wordCard.voice: The way of the Church. Redemptor Hominis 14: the human person, each one, is the road the Church must travel.

orig.note: Latin for way or road: the word for the Church's path in the encyclical's Latin.

carryVoice: Hold onto this: the person is the way, with no shortcut around anyone. Two weeks of the council's pages, done.

sources.work: Second Vatican Council, Gaudium et Spes
